data.gender_notes: Eranna is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Eranna is a Sanskrit name derived from the word ‘Eran’, meaning ‘earth’. This name is associated with Lord Shiva, who is believed to be the lord of the earth. Eranna is a powerful and grounding name, symbolizing strength, stability, and a deep connection to the natural world. The name Eranna carries the meaning “Lord of the Earth” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Eranna usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of the earth and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Eranna belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of the Earth.”

data.cultural_impact: Eranna holds cultural significance as a strong and grounding name, rooted in Hindu mythology. It represents a deep connection to nature, symbolizing stability, strength, and resilience. In some regions of India, it is also a common name for children born during agricultural seasons, as the earth is believed to be especially nurturing during these times.
data.spiritual_significance: Spiritually, Eranna is a powerful name, representing a deep connection to the divine energies of the earth and the mother goddess. In Hinduism, Lord Shiva is often depicted as a restorative and transformative force, rooted in the earth and transforming all experiences into spiritual growth. Eranna thus embodies the qualities of Lord Shiva, imparting strength, resilience, and a deep connection to the divine within.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Eranna: The radiant one, the embodiment of joy and happiness. It is a name evoking the essence of life's sunny side and the celebration of the divine within.

historical_references.reference: Eranna was a Jaina Tirthankara of the 12th nayakas or Tirthankaras in the present half of the 24 Tirthankaras cycle.
